title: Secure analytics view access controls and query-level permissions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Console analytics expose a variety of aggregate and time-series usage views (per-token cost, route latency, model usage, embeddings volume). Today these endpoints return full datasets to any user with general console read access. Problem: customers with multiple teams/orgs need fine-grained controls to ensure analysts only see data for the orgs/projects they manage; in some cases legal/compliance requires masking or blocking access to usage rows containing billing tokens or PII. Goal: implement query-level permission enforcement and view scoping in the console backend and analytics pipeline so that analytics REST endpoints and materialized views only return rows the requesting principal is authorized to see. Non-goal: redesign the metrics schema or change what raw telemetry we collect.
acceptance_criteria: Backend middleware enforces org/project scoping for all analytics endpoints (aggregate + timeseries)
Materialized views used by the console have schema-level privacy flags and are filtered during query time according to role mappings
Role definitions (OrgAdmin, OrgBilling, OrgAnalyst, ReadOnly) are documented and can be mapped to SSO groups and API tokens
All changes covered by unit and integration tests; load test shows <10% p50 latency regression for typical queries
Audit logs record the principal, query id, scope filters applied, and response size for every analytics request and are retained for 90 days
comments: 2025-02-15 Aisha Patel: Kickoff - scoped work with PM and security. Decided to implement a query-scoping layer in the console-api service and push filter predicates down to materialized views to keep runtime cost low.
2025-02-17 Diego Marin: Prototype middleware in console-api that reads principal.scope and injects where clauses. Prototype demo attached to PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2143

2025-02-19 Security Review (Nina Cho): Concern about downstream analytics pipeline (BigQuery) exposing billing tokens. Action: add a masking step and deny-list columns at the materialized view level. Raised security checklist item for KMS key access.

2025-02-21 PM sync (Jon Park): Prioritize OrgBilling role so finance teams can access cost breakdowns but not developer traces. PM requested a small CSV export permission flag separate from full dataset access.
2025-02-24 Diego Marin: Integrated with RBAC service endpoint /v1/roles/resolve. Implemented a cache with 5m TTL for role mappings. Measured single-request median added latency ~12ms on dev cluster.
2025-02-26 QA (Lina Gomez): Found flake where nested project-scoping was not applied for monthly rollups. Created ENG-8600 to enforce query scoping in warehouse queries.
2025-02-28 Aisha Patel: Security signoff on masking strategy pending one small change to retention config. Preparing rollout plan with feature flag 'analytics-strict-scope' for canary.
audit_requirements: Record principal id, role resolution path, applied scope filters, query fingerprint, response row count. Store in immutable append-only S3 path with 90-day lifecycle. Logs must be queryable by security and customer support teams.
migration_plan: 1) Add new privacy flags to materialized view definitions; deploy to warehouse under feature flag. 2) Deploy console-api middleware that sends 'scope_filter' with queries. 3) Run backfill job to mark legacy rows requiring masking. 4) Enable 'analytics-strict-scope' flag for 5% of traffic, monitor errors and latency for 48h, then 25%, then 100%.
testing_plan: Unit tests for middleware and role resolution. Integration tests using test warehouse with sample org/project dataset (see ENG-8601). Load test synthetic queries at production QPS in staging (target p95 < 2x baseline). End-to-end QA with sample SSO groups mapping to roles.
rollout_strategy: Behind feature flag 'analytics-strict-scope'. Canary 5% for one org, 48h observability window (error rate, query latency, false negatives). If no regression, ramp to 25% then 100% over one week. Rollback toggle ready if customer impact observed.
implementation_notes:
- Use existing RBAC service API for role resolution; do not duplicate mapping logic.
- Push simple predicate strings to warehouse queries to avoid large data transfers.
- For exported CSVs create a separate permission 'analytics.export' that is only granted to OrgAdmin/OrgBilling.
- Mask billing_token, user_email columns at view level for roles without billing access.
- Add new metric 'analytics.auth.filter_applied' to monitor % of queries using scoped filters.
qa_checklist: Role mapping resolves correctly for SSO groups and API tokens
Scoped queries return no rows outside permitted projects
Audit entries present for each analytics request
No PII columns present in responses for low-privilege roles
